TITLE: Tech View – No Six-Dot Drag Grip on Rows or Group Headers
TYPE: Story Defect · PARENT: SV-10052 (Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns; Ready for QA, read live 15 Oct 2026 12:28 UTC — re-read before the ask) · PRIORITY: Medium · LINK: relates to SV-10052 · relates to SV-10045 · LABEL: board-tech-view
ALREADY REPORTED: SV-11320 "Tech View: drag grip on every work order row and group header" (Open, Bug under epic SV-10043, reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward; read live 15 Oct 2026 12:30 UTC). A new ticket would repeat it. Suggested instead: link the failed test(s) to SV-11320 and file nothing new — the QA lead decides.
SEEN ON: staging build {{v26.40.17-a5c4210}}, 15 Oct 2026 (run 498).
PICTURES: the existing annotated staging pictures (banner on each), landscape; most were captured at 1x, so per Rule 116 re-take them at 2x before filing and run size_pics.py after the description write.
STATUS: DRAFT — NOT FILED. One ask per ticket; the QA lead decides (Rule 62/113).

h2. Description

*Every Tech View row and group header, Unassigned included, should show the six-dot drag grip at its left edge* to a user who can drag. On staging none shows.

For example,
* the Unassigned group header starts with the arrow, not the grip
* the work order rows start with the On Site pin; no row shows a grip

This appears inconsistent with the requirement defined in *Epic SV-10043* (Story *SV-10052*), the PRD and the design.

h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Sign in to staging as an Admin, check the top bar shows *Staging Heavy Duty - 9919*, and use a browser window 1440 px wide at 100% zoom.
# Open *Work Orders*, click the *All* tab, then *Tech View* in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar).
#* The group headers start with the arrow and the rows with the On Site pin; there is no six-dot grip anywhere.

*Actual Result:*
* No six-dot grip on any row or group header.

*Expected Result:*
* Every row and group header shows the grip, as the tests expect: *"Step 2: every group header, the Unassigned header too, shows a six-dot grip (two columns of three small grey dots) at its left edge, as in the design pictures."*
